intro: You are triaging real system logs from the Blue Gene/L supercomputer, cut into {n} windows of {lines} consecutive lines each, with one log line per row showing its timestamp, node location, component and level. For every window, list the alert categories that occur in it; most windows contain no alert. The alert rules below are exact: a line is an alert only if its component, level and message all match one category's rule, so a line's severity alone (FATAL, FAILURE, ERROR, SEVERE) does not make it an alert.
rules_intro: The rulebook table gives, for each rule, the category id, the component, the level and the message signature. A message signature is a regular expression searched in the message text: ^ anchors the start, $ anchors the end, and .* matches anything.

categories.KERNDTLB: A node kernel hit a fatal data-address translation hardware error.
categories.KERNTLBE: A node kernel hit a fatal instruction-address translation hardware error.
categories.KERNSTOR: A node kernel took a fatal storage access fault while running.
categories.KERNMNTF: A Lustre filesystem mount failed on a node during startup or I/O setup.
categories.KERNMNT: A node could not mount a required filesystem.
categories.KERNTERM: The runtime system terminated a node kernel after a fatal internal condition.
categories.KERNRTSP: The runtime system panicked and stopped execution on a node.
categories.KERNRTSA: A runtime-system assertion failed on a node, indicating inconsistent kernel state.
categories.KERNREC: A node kernel failed while receiving a packet on the tree network.
categories.KERNMICRO: The microloader asserted while bringing up node kernel code.
categories.KERNMC: A node reported a machine-check condition from processor or DDR memory hardware.
categories.KERNSOCK: A mailbox/control communication socket closed unexpectedly on a node.
categories.KERNCON: A node lost its connection to a node, link or service card after a packet timeout.
categories.KERNPOW: Power was deactivated for part of the machine.
categories.KERNSERV: A power-good signal dropped on hardware, indicating service may be required.
categories.KERNNOETH: A node lost its Ethernet link.
categories.KERNPROG: A node kernel took a fatal program interrupt.
categories.KERNFLOAT: A node kernel found floating-point hardware unavailable when it was needed.
categories.KERNEXT: A node took an external interrupt tied to a tree-network header with no waiting target.
categories.KERNBIT: DDR memory redundant bit steering failed on a node.
categories.APPTORUS: An application-level fatal message reported an uncorrectable torus network error.
categories.APPSEV: The ciod I/O daemon lost a control connection because the link was severed.
categories.APPRES: The ciod I/O daemon had a control connection reset by the peer.
categories.APPTO: The ciod I/O daemon timed out while reading from a control connection.
categories.APPREAD: The ciod I/O daemon failed to read a message prefix on a control stream.
categories.APPOUT: The ciod I/O daemon could not change into a login working directory because of an I/O error.
categories.APPUNAV: The ciod I/O daemon could not build a node map because a needed resource was temporarily unavailable.
categories.APPBUSY: The ciod I/O daemon could not build a node map because the device or resource was busy.
categories.APPCHILD: The ciod I/O daemon could not build a node map because no child processes were available.
categories.APPALLOC: The ciod I/O daemon could not build a node map because memory could not be allocated.
categories.LINKIAP: A link card failed an IAP operation while receiving or training a link.
categories.LINKDISC: A link card found a port disconnected during link operation.
categories.LINKPAP: A link card failed parity alignment on a port.
categories.LINKBLL: A link card failed to clear a port.
categories.MASABNORM: The master control server process exited abnormally because of a signal.
categories.MASNORM: The master control server process exited normally but was still logged as a failure-level event.
categories.MONPOW: The monitor failed because a power module was missing or unsupported.
categories.MONNULL: The monitor hit a Java NullPointerException while inserting monitoring data into the database.
categories.MMCS: The MMCS management subsystem reported a major internal error.

tools.list_windows: Lists window ids with their first and last timestamp, paged, returning at most 200 windows per call.
tools.read_window: Returns the numbered lines of one window, with optional start line and line count for paging, and output capped at about 8,000 characters.

answer: The final answer is one JSON object whose keys are the ids of windows that contain at least one alert and whose values are lists of the alert category ids present in that window, for example {example}; windows that are left out count as containing no alert.
score: The score is the F1 score over all (window, category) pairs in the answer compared with the true pairs.
unit_prompt: Triage exactly one window, {window}, using the same tools and the rulebook placed at {rules}; inspect the window, apply the rules exactly, and end with exactly one final line of the literal form UNIT | {window2} | <comma-separated category ids, or NONE>, where {window2} is the same id as {window}.
